author: A Robot
objectives: Determine steric number and predict electron-domain geometry.
Explain the impact of lone pairs on bond angles and molecular shape.
Compare VSEPR predictions with experimental observations.

modules.description: Introduction to electron domains and basic geometries.
modules.author: A Robot
educationalObjectives: Identify electron-domain geometries for simple molecules.

clips.changeMeaning: Spawn the central atom at the center of the workspace to demonstrate electron-pair repulsion principles visually.
clips.narration: Welcome. VSEPR theory states that electron pairs around a central atom will arrange themselves to minimize mutual repulsion. Watch as these domains space out.

clips.changeMeaning: Animate the transition of electron domains by scaling and updating the text label to show the tetrahedral geometry.
clips.narration: With a steric number of 4, the domains assume a tetrahedral geometry to keep as far apart as possible, at bond angles of 109.5 degrees.

modules.description: Differentiating molecular shape from electron-domain geometry.
modules.author: A Robot
educationalObjectives: Distinguish between electron-domain and molecular geometry.
Explain why bond angles deviate from ideal values due to lone pairs.

clips.changeMeaning: Highlight the difference between bonding and lone pairs in water by changing the central atom color to emphasize the lone pair electron density.
clips.narration: In water, the two lone pairs on oxygen occupy more angular space than bonding pairs, compressing the H-O-H bond angle to 104.5 degrees.

clips.changeMeaning: Visually represent the molecular geometry versus electron geometry by updating the text label description clearly.
clips.narration: While the electron geometry is tetrahedral, the molecular geometry is 'bent' because we only observe the positions of the atoms, not the lone pairs.

modules.description: Survey of higher steric number geometries.
modules.author: A Robot
educationalObjectives: Identify trigonal bipyramidal and octahedral geometries.
Apply VSEPR to complex molecules like XeF4.

clips.changeMeaning: Display complex geometries side by side to illustrate how different steric numbers lead to distinct spatial arrangements.
clips.narration: Finally, with steric numbers of 5 and 6, we observe trigonal bipyramidal and octahedral arrangements. These lead to shapes like seesaw, T-shaped, and square planar.
